en.title: Taxis and cars
en.summary: Taking a taxi, hiring a car and talking about driving.

paragraphs: Taxis and hire cars are useful when public transport is not enough. In this lesson you will tell a driver where to go, ask about price and discuss driving rules.
A passenger takes a taxi from a hotel in London to the airport.

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: No problem. It will take about forty minutes, depending on the traffic.

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Around sixty pounds. The meter will show the exact price.

lines.speaker: Passenger
lines.text: Could you stop at a cash machine on the way?

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Of course. There is one on the next corner.

lines.speaker: Passenger
lines.text: Thank you. Could you also help me with my suitcase?

paragraphs: **1. Will for predictions and estimates.** Will + base verb says what you expect to happen. It will take about forty minutes is an estimate. See Introduction to Grammar: Future and other tenses.

blocks.html:
FormExample
It will takeIt will take forty minutes.
It will costIt will cost around sixty pounds.
It won't beIt won't be long.
Will it be...?Will it be expensive?

paragraphs: **2. Prepositions give the destination and the stop.** To names the destination, at names the exact point, and on the way means during the journey. See Introduction to Grammar: Prepositions and conjunctions.

blocks.html:
PrepositionExample
toTo the airport, please.
atDrop me at the corner.
on the wayStop at a cash machine on the way.
outsideStop outside the hotel.

items: A black cab is the traditional London taxi, and many people book a taxi by phone app.
Hire a car is British; rent a car is American.
The meter shows the fare; the fare is the price of the journey.
Seat belt is required by law for all passengers in Britain and most US states.

paragraphs: Traffic keeps to the left in Britain and to the right in the United States, so a driver from abroad needs a few days to get used to it. In the United States tipping a taxi driver around fifteen percent is usual.
